metadata.title: Sione Vaki a Running Back to Avoid in Tough Week 11 Matchup
metadata.description: Detroit Lions running back Sione Vaki (ankle) is officially listed as questionable to play in his team's Week 11 matchup against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers due to a lingering ankle injury. Vaki has been able to play through the injury in each of the past two weeks, so he may be on track to do the same on Sunday. However, the 25-year-old is unlikely to see a significant workload as the Lions' RB2 behind star back Jahmyr Gibbs. Vaki also has a very difficult matchup against Tampa Bay, whose defense currently ranks second in the NFL in yards per carry allowed (3.4) and 1st in rushing touchdowns allowed (three). Vaki remains a worthy handcuff running back stash, but he should be avoided by fantasy managers in Week 11.

metadata.title: Sione Vaki Remains a Deep-League Handcuff at Running Back
metadata.description: Detroit Lions running back Sione Vaki had one of his better all-around games this year in the team's 35-10 win over the New England Patriots on Sunday in Munich, Germany, totaling 45 scrimmage yards on seven touches while watching lead back Jahmyr Gibbs dominate with 252 scrimmage yards and three touchdowns on 29 total touches. Vaki played 25% of the offensive snaps and carried the ball six times for 28 yards (4.7 yards per carry) while catching his only target for a 17-yard gain. While not seeing much volume -- 36 carries for 163 yards and eight catches for 81 yards behind the workhorse Gibbs -- the former fourth-rounder from Utah has been efficient with his limited opportunities in Detroit's backfield, averaging a career-high 4.5 yards per carry and 10.1 yards per reception in nine games played in his third year in the NFL. Vaki does not have any standalone fantasy value as long as Gibbs is healthy, but he remains a deep-league handcuff option at RB for managers who are lucky enough to have Gibbs on their roster. If anything were to happen to Gibbs, Vaki would be in line for a massive boost in volume in one of the highest-scoring offenses in the league. Right now, Vaki is only rostered in 1% of Yahoo leagues.

The Lions may look to lean on the run game in Week 9 against the Miami Dolphins, although Miami's defense currently ranks 10th in the NFL in yards per carry allowed (3.8). metadata.title: Sione Vaki Unlikely to See Significant Workload in Week 8
metadata.description: Despite holding his team's RB2 role, Detroit Lions running back Sione Vaki has played a minimal role on offense in 2026. Across six games, the 25-year-old has recorded 108 yards from scrimmage on 20 touches. The Lions have leaned very heavily on star RB1 Jahmyr Gibbs, leaving very little opportunity for Vaki to rack up fantasy-relevant production. Gibbs missed practice on Wednesday of this week with a shoulder injury, but he returned to full participation on both Thursday and Friday and is off the injury report heading into Detroit's Week 8 matchup against the Minnesota Vikings. Vaki may see a few extra touches if Gibbs is battling a minor injury, but Minnesota has been one of the best defenses in football in 2026 and enters Week 8 ranked third in the NFL in total rushing yards allowed (587). All in all, Vaki should not be in starting consideration for fantasy managers on Sunday against the Vikings.

metadata.title: Sione Vaki Remains Tough to Trust in Week 7

metadata.title: Sione Vaki Carries Shaky Standalone Value in Week 5

Arizona also currently ranks 32nd in the NFL in yards per pass attempt allowed, which could lead to lower rush volume in general for the Lions. Vaki is worth stashing as a handcuff running back, but he remains tough for fantasy managers to trust as a starter in Week 5.

metadata.title: Sione Vaki Remains Tough to Rely on in Week 4 Despite Increasing Usage
metadata.description: Detroit Lions running back Sione Vaki has seen little involvement in his team's offense so far in 2026, recording 75 scrimmage yards on 12 touches across three games. However, the 25-year-old had his usage scaled up in Detroit's Week 3 win over the New York Jets, recording six carries for 26 yards and an 11-yard reception while playing a season-high 31% of his team's offensive snaps. As long as superstar Lions back Jahmyr Gibbs remains healthy, Vaki's production upside is limited. Still, Gibbs currently leads the NFL in touches, which may not be sustainable if Detroit hopes to keep him healthy throughout an 18-week season. If he sees another small bump in workload, Vaki could have some chances to score fantasy points in his Week 4 matchup against the Panthers. Carolina has had trouble against the run early on, allowing an NFL-worst 5.7 yards per carry and six total rushing touchdowns through three games. Vaki should not yet be trusted as a starter, but he could be worth stashing in deeper league formats.

metadata.title: Sione Vaki Hard to Trust as More than a Stash Option in Week 3

However, Detroit has given Gibbs the vast majority of its backfield work so far this season, utilizing Vaki mostly as a pass-protector for quarterback Jared Goff. Vaki has almost no history of being an impactful offensive player, as he has recorded just 15 touches across 29 career games with the Lions. While the 25-year-old carries some stash appeal in deeper fantasy leagues as a handcuff running back option, Vaki should likely remain on the bench for fantasy managers in his Week 3 matchup against the New York Jets.

metadata.title: Sione Vaki Moves Into Handcuff Territory
metadata.description: Detroit Lions running back Sione Vaki is not getting enough touches to help fantasy lineups, but his spot in the backfield suddenly matters a lot more. Vaki has three carries for 14 yards and two catches for 24 yards through two games, including 20 total yards on two touches against Buffalo. Detroit now lists him directly behind Jahmyr Gibbs on the depth chart, with Jacob Saylors third. Isiah Pacheco (back) is also expected to miss significant time after undergoing surgery, so this does not look like a temporary one-week opening. Gibbs is still handling a massive share of the backfield work, which leaves Vaki without much standalone value. The appeal is what happens if Gibbs ever misses time. RotoBaller includes Vaki among its high-upside handcuffs and recommends him in 14-team PPR leagues. He is a deep bench stash right now, but the path to a much larger role is clearer than his five touches through two games would suggest.

metadata.title: Sione Vaki Remains a Risky Start in Week 2 Despite Emerging Role in Detroit
metadata.description: Detroit Lions running back Sione Vaki emerged as his team's RB2 in Week 1, playing 29% of Detroit's offensive snaps in its overtime win over the New Orleans Saints. With Lions running back Isiah Pacheco (back, knee) expected to miss three-plus months after undergoing back surgery, Vaki could have an extended runway as the primary backup to star Lions back Jahmyr Gibbs. However, Vaki still projects to play a limited role on offense, as he recorded two carries for seven yards and one catch for 11 yards in Week 1. With Gibbs fully healthy heading into Detroit's matchup against the Buffalo Bills on Thursday Night Football, RotoBaller ranks Vaki as the RB68 in Week 2. Deeper-league managers may want to consider stashing Vaki off the waiver wire for his handcuff appeal, but he's not worthy of starting consideration against the Bills.

metadata.title: Sione Vaki Emerging as Detroit's No. 2 Back
metadata.description: Detroit Lions running back Sione Vaki only had three touches in Sunday's 31-30 overtime win over New Orleans, but his playing time made the bigger statement. Vaki carried twice for seven yards and caught his only target for 11 more while logging 22 offensive snaps. Jacob Saylors did not play an offensive snap, and Detroit's current depth chart now lists Vaki second behind Jahmyr Gibbs. That matters even more after Isiah Pacheco underwent back surgery and was given an estimated 12-week recovery timeline. Gibbs is still going to dominate this backfield after handling 34 touches in the opener, so Vaki has little immediate starting value. The path behind him is much cleaner than it looked a week ago, though. Vaki still needs to improve after an uneven opener, particularly in pass protection, but he has the first crack at the reserve role while Pacheco is sidelined. He is worth stashing in 14-team PPR leagues and deeper formats before Detroit's backfield hierarchy becomes more settled.

metadata.title: Sione Vaki Has a Path to Week 1 Touches
metadata.description: Detroit Lions running back Sione Vaki has a little more life as a deep-league stash with Isiah Pacheco on injured reserve. Dan Campbell said Vaki and Jacob Saylors will split the No. 2 role behind Jahmyr Gibbs against New Orleans, so there is no clean handcuff here. Still, Vaki has earned some trust. Campbell liked the progress he made as both a runner and pass catcher during camp and said he is comfortable using him when Gibbs needs a breather. The problem is we have barely seen Vaki on offense in the NFL. He has seven career carries for 18 yards and three catches for 37 yards, while Saylors is going to get work too. Vaki is rostered in only 1% of Yahoo leagues and sits in the 14-team PPR range on the current waiver list. That makes him more of a cheap bench swing than someone to start in Week 1.

metadata.title: Sione Vaki - Committee approach at RB2
metadata.description: Coach Dan Campbell said Monday that neither Vaki nor Jacob Saylors is viewed as the Lions' strict RB2, and Detroit will use a committee approach behind Jahmyr Gibbs, Nolan Bianchi of The Detroit News reports.
metadata.analysis: Isiah Pacheco was signed over the offseason to serve as the Lions' RB2 behind Gibbs, but he injured his back and is opening the regular season on injured reserve. Pacheco remains without a firm timetable for return, so it's Vaki and Saylors who will see elevated roles on game days. The inexperienced duo has combined for nine career regular-season carries. Gibbs is expected to have a heavy 2026 workload with David Montgomery out of town and now with the Texans.

metadata.title: Sione Vaki - Elevated role sans Pacheco
metadata.description: Vaki is in line to operate in an elevated offensive role to open the regular season after Isiah Pacheco (back) was placed on injured reserve Tuesday, Tim Twentyman of the Lions' official site reports.
metadata.analysis: Vaki and Jacob Saylors are the two healthy backup running backs on the roster behind Jahmyr Gibbs following Pacheco's placement on IR. Vaki has mostly operated on special teams since entering the league in 2024 as a fourth-round pick, but he'll have the opportunity to rotate with Saylors behind Gibbs for as long as Pacheco is shelved.
